case_analysis.thread_summary: This long thread (July 2024 - November 29, 2024) traces the full lifecycle of a proxy Bluetooth SIG registration for New Cosmos Electric (新コスモス電機), a returning customer (contact: Azuma), for a sensor product using a newly-adopted Nordic nRF52/SD140 BLE module. It begins with an initial inquiry covering (1) registration for a new BLE module and (2) adding a model to a prior registration, proceeds through quote negotiation (two-group fee breakdown: registration support/Compliance Folder vs. USD remittance proxy/Qualification Fee), internal approval delays, USD remittance and SIG fee confirmation, and completion of the proxy registration confirmation form. Mid-process, the customer asks about the mandatory 'brief English product description' field and registration publication-date strategy for an unreleased sensor product. A major sub-thread covers SIG account/login problems (departed employee's account, Get Username/password reset, and a 'Transfer Request' to move the Qualification Fee Receipt Number to a new account). Another sub-thread resolves a SoftDevice version mismatch (S140 6.1.1 vs actual 7.2.0) by referencing different Component QDIDs via an End Product registration covering multiple versions. The customer then asks about a yellow ICS Form warning and TCW (Test Case Waiver), which Sakai explains in detail as a 'phantom inconsistency' caused by referencing pre-2019 QDIDs against the current ICS structure. After customer sign-off on the review page, registration is finalized, My Page access is shared, Compliance Folder materials (for one representative model, NXA-S) are collected, and the Compliance Folder (CD-R) is shipped via Click Post with standard retention/audit/derivative-registration guidance.
all_questions_found: What is the fee breakdown for proxy registration support, Compliance Folder creation, USD remittance proxy, and Qualification Fee, and what is the end-to-end timeline?
Is the 'brief English product description' field mandatory, and how detailed should it be for an unreleased sensor product? Can we use a publication date to avoid early disclosure?
Why can't Allion log into our SIG account with the credentials we provided, and how do we resolve account/Receipt Number ownership issues after switching to a new account?
Our actual SoftDevice version (S140 7.2.0) differs from what was quoted (6.1.1) and has no direct Component registration - which QDIDs should the new registration reference?
Why does the ICS Form show a yellow warning for this QDID combination, and what does 'acceptable via TCW' mean?
What Compliance Folder materials do we need to provide (can one model's materials suffice for a multi-model Product List), how is it delivered, and what about future derivative models?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The registration referenced Component QDIDs for a Nordic nRF52 module's Link Layer and Host stack (SoftDevice S140). A version discrepancy (quoted as 6.1.1, actually 7.2.0) was resolved by identifying an End Product registration (QDID:138767, 'nRF52 Series with SD140 v7.2.0') whose Product List had been expanded from 7.0.1 to also cover 7.2.0 and 7.3.0, and referencing the same underlying Component QDIDs (at their 7.0.1 registration) that this End Product registration used. Referencing these 2019-vintage (Core Spec v5.1) QDIDs against the current ICS structure produced 10 LL>GAP conditional-mandatory consistency-check warnings, because newer ICS items (GAP 8/3, 8/4, 20/5, 20/6, 20/7; CORE 40/3) trigger requirements for LL items (3/1a, 3/4b, 3/5a) that don't exist in the old QDIDs' ICS at all - 'phantom inconsistency items' resolvable via TCW. Account/credential issues arose because the SIG member account (needed for both Invoice/Receipt Number and registration login) was tied to a departed employee; a new account was created and the Qualification Fee Receipt Number was moved to it via a SIG 'Transfer Request' with email-based 'Accept' confirmation. The mandatory English product description (published verbatim to SIG's certified-products list) was kept generic for the unreleased sensor product, paired with a specified publication date to delay disclosure.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Quoting separated registration-related fees from payment-related fees (remittance proxy + Qualification Fee in USD), with a two-phase timeline (remittance/confirmation ~2-3 weeks, then registration 1-3 business days). For module version mismatches, the decision process traced from the customer's actual version to an End Product registration covering that version, then back to the underlying Component QDIDs to reference. ICS consistency warnings from referencing older QDIDs were diagnosed structurally (mapping old ICS onto new ICS structure) before resolving via TCW rather than assuming a real conformance gap. Account issues were resolved by verifying the login account matched the Invoice-obtaining account, then using SIG's Transfer Request mechanism when a new account was needed. Public-facing registration fields (product description) were kept generic for unreleased products, combined with a specified publication date for disclosure control.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Incorrect QDID references due to an unresolved SoftDevice version mismatch could misrepresent the product's certified configuration. Misreading an ICS consistency-check warning as a real functional gap (instead of a phantom/structural artifact) could cause unnecessary delays or rework, while failing to apply for a needed TCW could block registration. Unresolved account/Receipt Number issues would prevent registration from proceeding at all. A detailed public product description for an unreleased sensor could prematurely reveal its function; failing to specify a publication date could expose registration details early. Requiring complete multi-model Compliance Folder documentation when unavailable could delay closeout.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For returning customers with newly-adopted modules, verify the actual SoftDevice/firmware version against SIG's site early, and if no direct Component registration exists for that version, trace through an End Product registration covering it to find the correct Component QDIDs to reference. When referencing older QDIDs triggers ICS consistency-check warnings, diagnose whether the flagged items are 'phantom' (didn't exist in the old QDID's original ICS) before applying for a TCW, and explain this distinction to the customer. Always confirm the SIG account used for proxy registration matches the Invoice/Receipt-Number-holding account, especially for returning customers whose original registrant may have left the company - use SIG's Transfer Request mechanism if a new account is needed. For unreleased products (especially sensors), recommend a generic public product description and a specified publication date to control disclosure timing. For Compliance Folders covering multi-model registrations, one representative model's materials can suffice if complete documentation for all models isn't available.
